title: Enquirer’s Guide: Are there places to explore on the other side?
summary: Surveyors speak of layers, not a single continuous landscape.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “Are there places to explore on the other side?”
Surveyors speak of layers, not a single continuous landscape.
A route is described by its layer, its relation to the Prime Referent, and a measured sonance offset. Familiar distances and compass directions cannot be trusted without further checks.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
